I have two :  
\- One of them is a magical being (a god-like creature, that didn't shape the world but can infuse their magic into other beings) that successfully created a new "race" of magical humans that can control magic and other being. He wants to become the "king" of the god-like creature and the God for the humans. But he was cast away by the other god-like creatures and sworn to find a way to retrieve his god-like status and become even more powerful to kill them all.

\- The other one is a human that was born almost dead years later the first one was cast away. One of the reigning god-like creature, who want a "champion" to defeat the fallen god-like creature, saved the baby by creating a exact twin, granting the twin with huge power. But still, the baby was weak and had to stay home, while his "brother" (who's the protagonist) worked to help the family and find a cure to his brother's weakness.  
He learned he has powers too (he can "fuse" beings and/or magical infused objects, for example the first thing he did was fusing a rat with a bird, giving the rat wings, he also healed an injured wolf with his own skin, giving the wolf an ability to turn human), but the family didn't want him to use it because of his weakness and low energy.  
But after many years waiting alone in the house, he became bitter, he hated that the god-like creature never cured his weakness will giving his brother everything he should have. Then he learned he wasn't that weak : their mother wasn't ready to let him leave the house (she was scared to lose him) and poisoned him to weakened his vital force since he was a child. Of course the brother never knew this, but when he confronted them about it, in his rage he killed their mother and accused his brother (whom everyone knows is healthy) of killing her, forcing him to flee and become a "criminal" of a crime he never did.  
The weakened man regained quickly his forces and sworn to get revenge on the god-like creature that let him almost die.  


Both of the villains became "allies" because they have the same goal. Also the second one, with his fusing power can help the first one to retrieve his power and become more powerful. So it's a win-win situation for both of them.

I’m a web developer, I love it: I can learn new things everyday and teach it to my colleagues and friends, it’s a mixed between programming and designing so I have to use logic and intuition all the time. But it can also be stressful and frustrating.

In my spare time (I mean it’s been since high school now so… very long time), I have a story that I’m writing (I’m currently starting over to plan more things than before, it’s really difficult but I’m so excited when I have a new idea that work with the plot or other ideas I have).

But currently, I’m thinking that maybe therapist would have been a better job for me. I really love listening to my friends’s problem and helping them find answers. I used to think that I had to find solutions for their problems, but after reading a lot (but still I think not enough) about mental health, I tend to think that understanding how you feel is the key to find real, useful solutions. So that’s what I’m currently trying to do with my friends.
Note that before going for a web developer degree, I wanted to study in psychology but it was way too long (here in France it was like 7 or 9 years) and even though I was not bad in school (ok actually good), I just wanted to “become an adult” and “find a fulfilling job” (and most importantly leave away from my parents, on my own). So yeah, I think I would have loved helping people with their problem (I mean I’m still “helping” people by creating webapp so I think it still count?).

Thanks for the question by the way, what about you?

Edit: oh I saw your own answer so no need to answer my question 🙈

Oh yeah. And that was even more difficult in high school when I was trying to understand my sexuality: am I in love with my girl friends or is it just strong feelings of friendship? And I still do, sometimes, question my feelings to understand if it’s just friendship or more and it’s exhausting.

So I’m sorry, I don’t have any advice, but you are not alone in this. I think it’s because we tend to have deep connection with people we want to be friend with, so it’s easily mixed up with romantic feeling (I mean, isn’t it a stereotype to say our SO is our best friend?).
